channel.title: SecOpsAI Security Blog
channel.description: Real-time SecOpsAI advisories, detections, mitigation steps, and incident updates.

item.title: SecOpsAI Daily Intelligence Brief — 2026-11-11
item.description: 8 separate advisories · 4 exploited in the wild · highest CVSS 9.5.

item.title: SecOpsAI Daily Intelligence Brief — 2026-11-10
item.description: IBM Aspera Faspex Incorrect Authorization Vulnerability (exploited); OpenBSD OpenSSH Unexpected Status Code or Return Value Vulnerability (exploited); node-opcua: Namespace-Level RBAC Fail-Open - Anonymous Write/Call Bypass via Unbound `DefaultRolePermissions; and 5 more.

item.title: SecOpsAI Daily Intelligence Brief — 2026-11-09
item.description: SonicWall SonicOS SSLVPN Use of Single-factor Authentication Vulnerability (exploited); fastapi-code-generator: Import-time RCE via response status-code key -> unescaped @app.get(..., responses={...}) dict; fastapi-code-generator: Import-time RCE via route path -> unescaped @app.get('...') decorator; and 2 more.

item.title: SecOpsAI Daily Intelligence Brief — 2026-11-08
item.description: LXD has argument injection in backup compression algorithm leading to AFW and ACE; LXD has arbitrary file write on client due to trusted image hash; LXD has restricted project bypass leading to arbitrary command execution.

item.title: SecOpsAI Daily Intelligence Brief — 2026-11-06
item.description: Ivanti Connect Secure Generation of Predictable Numbers or Identifiers Vulnerability (exploited); Banks: Unsafe importlib.import_module of attacker-controlled Tool.import_path in CompletionExtension allows RCE; GitPython: arbitrary file read via attacker-controlled branch name in `Head.checkout()` (incomplete fix of CVE-2026-78679); and 1 more.

item.description: Verified intelligence and defensive updates for 2026-11-03.

item.description: Verified intelligence and defensive updates for 2026-10-31.

item.title: Measuring a malicious-package funnel: from 13% to 39% recall at under 0.5% false positives
item.description: Public signatures caught 13% of 3,055 confirmed malicious packages. SecOpsAI behaviour rules, built from what they missed, raised that to 39% while flagging under 0.5% of popular packages.

item.title: Anatomy of a false positive: clearing a critical npm alert in twenty minutes
item.description: SecOpsAI scored a benign desktop-assistant release 100/100. A release diff, install-hook review and rule-by-rule explanation cleared it, and exposed two scoring flaws we have now fixed.

item.title: Mini Shai-Hulud crosses npm and PyPI: advisory protection for removed artifacts
item.description: Mini Shai-Hulud affected npm and PyPI packages, including removed artifacts that now receive source-backed SecOpsAI advisory detections.
